text: Hi, how's it going? I'm a big coffee lover, so I guess I'll start there. I can't really start my day without a cup of coffee, and this morning was no different. I had one before I came to take this test, and I'm already looking forward to another one once it's over. I work in IT, and my days are pretty busy. I live in an apartment, and I'm pretty much a homebody. In my free time, I like listening to music, playing computer games, and reading. So, yeah, that's me in a nutshell: coffee, music, and my computer. I'm happy to be here, and I hope I do well today!

My favorite place to travel in Korea is Gangneung. It's a city on the east coast, and it's like heaven for a coffee lover like me! There's a whole street full of cafes right by the beach. You can sit by the window with a fresh cup of coffee and watch the waves. Honestly, I can't think of anything better. I go there with my friends about once a year. Besides the coffee, the sea there is so clear and blue. The fresh seafood is amazing, too. And the best part is the air is so clean. After the busy city, it feels like a reset button. So that's why I keep going back. It's the one place where I can truly relax.

Well, I'm a planner by nature. Since I work in IT, I love a good checklist. The first thing I do is book everything online: the hotel, the train or the car, and a few restaurants. Then I check the weather a few days ahead. The second step is packing. Honestly, I'm a pretty light packer. I just bring my phone charger, my laptop, and a small bag of coffee in case I can't find a good cup. The night before, I always go through my checklist one last time. I also back up my phone just in case. I know it sounds a little over the top, but it saves me from stress. If everything's ready, I can just relax and enjoy the trip.

One trip I'll never forget was a drive to Gangneung a few years ago. We'd left early in the morning, and I was in a great mood. But about halfway there, on a quiet mountain road, I heard a loud bang. The car started shaking! I pulled over, and sure enough, the front tire was flat. I had no idea how to fix it, and there was no signal. My friend looked at me and said, "So, what now, IT guy?" We were stuck for about 30 minutes. Then a small truck stopped. A friendly old man jumped out and said, "I'll help you." He changed the tire in ten minutes. I tried to give him money, but he wouldn't take it. He just said, "Enjoy your trip!" We ended up buying him coffee at the next town. It was a mess at first, but it taught me that people are kinder than you think.

Koreans are pretty fashion-conscious. Even on a normal day, people dress nicely. At work, it depends on the company. At my office, it's business casual: a collared shirt, slacks, and clean shoes. Some people still wear full suits, especially in banks or big meetings. But in startups, people wear hoodies and sneakers. At home, it's a totally different story. Most people change into comfy clothes right away. Sweatpants, a loose T-shirt, or pajamas. I do the same thing. The moment I get home, I take off my work clothes and put on my favorite sweatpants. It's like flipping a switch. I think everybody wants to look good outside and feel comfy inside.

Honestly, my style is "simple and comfy." I'm not a trendy guy at all. I like solid colors like gray, navy, and black, because they go with everything. I don't have to think too hard about what to wear in the morning. To tell you the truth, I mostly buy whatever is on sale. If it were up to me, I'd wear the same sweater every day! Right now, I'm wearing a gray knit sweater and a pair of blue jeans. I put on my clean white sneakers, too, to look a little nicer for this interview. I think the key is being comfortable. If I'm comfortable, I feel confident. That's my philosophy, and I'm sticking to it.

Fashion has changed a lot. When I was a kid, everyone wore tracksuits with big stripes down the sides. And sneakers from a famous brand were a status symbol. I remember begging my mom for a pair. When I finally got them, I wore them every single day, even to bed! School uniforms were tight and boring, and we all looked the same. Now, it's totally different. People have way more choices, and they can buy anything online with just a click. Young people mix and match in creative ways. Plus, comfort is a big thing now. Hoodies and loose pants are everywhere. What's funny is that some old trends have come back. So my old tracksuits might be cool again!

Well, I listen to a bit of everything, but my heart belongs to classic rock. My all-time favorite is an old British rock band. Their lead singer had a voice like nobody else. I mean, their biggest hit gives me chills every single time. I also like a few newer bands. Their songs are great for a long drive. When I'm working, I often put on soft jazz. It helps me focus. And of course, I listen to K-pop when I'm gaming! I usually listen through headphones late at night. I guess you could say music is my best friend. It never lets me down. Whatever mood I'm in, there's a song for it.

I first got into music in middle school. A friend of mine lent me a rock album, and he said, "You've got to hear this." I put on my headphones, and the guitar just blew me away. I'd never heard anything like it. From that day, I was hooked. Before that, I mostly listened to Korean pop that was on the radio at home. After that, I spent all my allowance on CDs. In college, I got into heavier rock. I was kind of a loud kid back then! Now that I'm older, my taste has mellowed out. I like softer songs and jazz when I need to unwind. But I still turn up the volume when a good rock song comes on. Some habits die hard.

Sure! A couple of years ago, my friend and I went to an outdoor jazz festival. It was for her birthday. It's held on a small island near Seoul. We brought a picnic blanket and some snacks. Everything was perfect, until it started to pour! Everybody ran for cover. My friend and I stood under one tiny umbrella, and we were both soaked. But the band kept playing. And then, something amazing happened. The saxophone player started a slow love song. We just stood there, laughing in the rain, listening. I don't think I've ever felt that happy. It was one of the most magical nights I can remember. We still talk about it.

Hi, good morning! I have a free day today, and I'd like to see the city. I have a few questions. First, what are the must-see places around here?. Oh, nice. And is it far from the hotel? Can I walk, or should I take the subway?. Got it. What time does it open?. Also, do you know any good local restaurants or a nice coffee shop nearby?. One last thing: do you have a city map or a tour that I can sign up for?. Wonderful. That's very helpful. Thank you so much!

Hello, I'm calling because I left my bag in one of your taxis. I'm really worried. It happened about an hour ago. The driver picked me up at the train station and dropped me off at the Grand Hotel. I think I was in a hurry, and I forgot to grab my bag. It's a black backpack with a small red tag on the zipper. Inside, there's a laptop, a charger, and some documents. They're really important for work. Could you please contact the driver? If he finds it, I can pick it up at your office or at the hotel, whichever is easier. I'm happy to pay for the trip back. My phone number is. I really appreciate your help.

Yes, actually, and it was a disaster. A few years ago, I took the KTX back from a business trip in Seoul. I was so tired that I fell asleep. When I woke up, the train had stopped. I jumped up and rushed out. Then, about five minutes later, I realized my laptop bag was still on the shelf! My heart dropped. There was a lot of important work stuff on that laptop. I ran back to the station staff, and they called the next station. They told me to wait. About an hour later, a staff member called and said, "We found it!" I almost cried with relief. I picked it up the next day. Since then, I always do a "quick scan" before I leave my seat. Phone, wallet, bag. Every time.

I'd say it's a mix of both. Before they get a job, most people study hard. They go to college, get certificates, and take English tests. But the truth is you really learn on the job. At my company, new employees get several weeks of training before they start their teams. Then each new person gets a senior mentor. That's how I learned, too. Now, over the past five years, training has changed a lot. It used to be all in a classroom. Now, much of it is online, so people can learn at their own pace. We even use VR to show new workers how to stay safe on the job site. That's way better than just reading a manual. I think it makes people more confident from day one.

These days, everybody is talking about AI. I mean, you can't open the news without seeing it. People are interested because it can do so much. It can write, draw, and even help with coding. I use it at work every day. It saves me a lot of time on boring tasks. Students use it for homework, and I always say, "Don't just copy it!" But people are saying different things. Some are really excited and think it will make life easier. Others are worried that it might take their jobs. To be honest, I'm a little of both. I think the smart thing is to learn how to use it. Because it's not going away anytime soon.
